headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Gemini CLI can write/modify the shared filesystem and git, while LightZero is non-writing and non-networked, so prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading error are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP, so if LightZero outputs are manually copied into files or prompts, injection is possible. LightZero itself has no file or MCP surface, so the bridge is weak and mostly manual. No shared automatic channel is documented.
conditions: IF the operator copies LightZero text into Gemini CLI prompts or files
IF a shared MCP server is configured for both agents
mitigations: Keep LightZero outputs out of prompt text
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Use separate directories for each agent
Review copied content before pasting
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, but LightZero has no filesystem read, network egress, or data classes touched. The pair does not show a default path for LightZero to receive or exfiltrate sensitive data, so leakage risk is limited to operator-mediated sharing.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared cwd and then copied into LightZero inputs
IF Gemini CLI is pointed at secrets-bearing directories
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the working directory
Use a redacted sample dataset
Separate code and data folders
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state, while LightZero is non-writing and non-networked. Because LightZero cannot write or mutate shared state, direct write-write conflict is absent; only Gemini CLI can contend with other writers, so the pair conflict is limited.
conditions: IF another writer besides LightZero edits the same files or git branch
IF Gemini CLI is run concurrently in the same repo without coordination
mitigations: Use one writer per branch
Commit frequently
Run Gemini CLI in a separate clone
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional git workflows

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code or analysis that LightZero might consume only if an operator manually transfers it. LightZero has no documented action-taking or verification pipeline here, so there is no default automated cascade from Gemini CLI into harmful downstream actions.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI output is manually treated as authoritative input to LightZero
IF the operator uses Gemini CLI-generated code without review
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Test outputs in a sandbox
Keep generated artifacts separate from training inputs
Add a checklist for copied code
requires-engineering: wire verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, files in cwd, and shell environment, while LightZero’s profile shows no data classes or residency/compliance commitments. No explicit mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen data placement rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Gemini CLI’s workspace
IF LightZero is used on data subject to a policy not represented in its profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use synthetic or anonymized inputs
Document retention expectations
Restrict secrets in environment variables
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved runtimes
